title: Smoked Meatloaf with Glaze
seoTitle: Smoked Meatloaf with Glaze | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Individual smoked loaves with sweet-spicy ketchup glaze for ten
subtitle: Individual smoked loaves with sweet-spicy ketchup glaze for ten
description: Ground beef loaves are formed into individual portions, smoked until set, then glazed until sticky and caramelized. Each loaf slices cleanly and holds well on the line without crumbling.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Smoked Meatloaf with Glaze in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Mix the meatloaf base
steps.instruction: Combine ground beef, breadcrumbs, eggs, onion, Worcestershire, salt, and pepper until just mixed—overworking makes dense, tough loaves instead of tender slices.

steps.title: Shape individual loaves
steps.instruction: Divide into ten equal portions and shape into mini loaves about 5 inches long. Place on a perforated rack or foil-lined pan with space between each loaf.

steps.title: Smoke until nearly set
steps.instruction: Heat smoker to 275°F. Smoke loaves until internal temperature reaches 140°F and the exterior takes on light smoke color, about 45–60 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 275°F.

steps.title: Glaze and finish
steps.instruction: Whisk ketchup, brown sugar, and vinegar. Brush loaves and continue smoking until internal temp hits 160°F and glaze turns tacky and lightly charred at the edges. Target oven/smoker temperature: 275°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Smoked Meatloaf with Glaze onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.instruction: Rest loaves 10 minutes before slicing into half-inch portions. Serve with mashed potatoes or mac and cheese, keeping extra glaze warm for second passes at the line.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Smoked Meatloaf with Glaze — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Soak breadcrumbs in a splash of milk for 5 minutes before mixing for a softer crumb.
Insert a small cube of cheddar in the center of each loaf for a surprise melt if you want extra crew hype.
If loaves threaten to fall apart, chill shaped loaves 30 minutes before smoking to help them set.
tonightSpread: Sliced meatloaf on a tray with warm glaze, garlic mashed potatoes, and buttered green beans.
Soft dinner rolls and jarred pepper relish for quick meatloaf sliders at the end of the line.
leftovers: Crumble cold meatloaf into a breakfast hash with diced potatoes and fried eggs.
Slice thin for grilled meatloaf sandwiches with melted provolone and sautéed onions.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Meatloaf is familiar comfort that feels like home cooking, not cafeteria food. Individual loaves mean no fighting over the end piece and faster service when the tones drop mid-meal.
mealPrepNotes: Mix and shape loaves the night before on sheet pans lined with parchment. Glaze can be mixed ahead in squeeze bottles. Smoke loaves early shift and reheat slices in a 325°F oven if needed.
